name: Neoconservatism
summary: Neoconservatism grew from American anti-Stalinist liberals who turned against the New Left and the Great Society and came to favor free-market growth, cultural traditionalism and an assertive foreign policy. It supports American military primacy, confrontation with hostile regimes, and promotion of democracy, with limited trust in international institutions. Domestically it accepts a reduced but real welfare state and treats culture and morality as political matters.
scope: The mainstream American movement from Irving Kristol, Norman Podhoretz and Jeane Kirkpatrick in the 1970s-80s to the Kristol-Kagan PNAC network and the Bush-era foreign policy. It does not cover the pre-1970s liberal-hawk precursors or non-American uses of the term.

furtherReading.title: The Neoconservative Persuasion by Irving Kristol
furtherReading.note: Kristol's own 2003 account of what neoconservatism is.

furtherReading.title: Dictatorships and Double Standards by Jeane Kirkpatrick
furtherReading.note: The 1979 essay that made her a neoconservative foreign-policy voice.

furtherReading.title: Project for the New American Century (Wikipedia)
furtherReading.note: The think tank behind the 1990s-2000s push for US primacy.

keyFigures.name: Irving Kristol
keyFigures.role: Called the godfather of neoconservatism; coined and popularized the label.

keyFigures.name: Norman Podhoretz
keyFigures.role: Editor of Commentary, which became a key neoconservative publication.

keyFigures.name: Jeane Kirkpatrick
keyFigures.role: Author of Dictatorships and Double Standards and Reagan's UN ambassador.

sources.usedFor: Kristol's two cheers for capitalism, supply-side, welfare views, imperial role remark.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Neoconservatives accept a limited welfare state on practical grounds and were never defined by health policy, so adherents split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not a defining issue; neoconservatives favor growth-first economics but did not campaign against wage floors as a matter of principle.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: They give a qualified endorsement of free markets, while holding that markets lack moral guidance.

public-ownership.rationale: Kristol and the Public Interest circle stressed the unintended harms of government planning and favored private enterprise.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Kristol describes neoconservatives as favoring lower tax rates to encourage growth.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from their anti-New Left, pro-growth stance; early figures came from the union-friendly anti-Stalinist left, so it is a soft view.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred from their endorsement of capitalism and natural rights; not a stated priority.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from their qualified pro-market position; they accept some regulation on practical grounds.

cut-welfare.rationale: They favor a reduced welfare state limited by practical rather than principled concerns, rejecting most Great Society programs but keeping the New Deal core.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: former socialists who broke with the left and embraced capitalism, with no sympathy for collective ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from their hawkish national-security stance after 2001.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from their concern about cultural decline and opposition to the counterculture.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: opposed to the speech-code politics of the left, though they favor regulating pornography and obscenity.

strong-leader.rationale: They favor a strong presidency in foreign affairs but have no doctrine of bypassing gridlock; adherents split.

state-harmful.rationale: Kristol rejects the limited-government case as a historical eccentricity and says people prefer strong government to weak government.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the movement's general outlook rather than stated; adherents are not uniform.

empower-police-military.rationale: Calls for large defense spending increases and a dominant military are central, and they stress law and order against the counterculture.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from their moral conservatism on cultural questions.

decide-locally.rationale: Inferred: they emphasize a strong national government and national purpose over devolution.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the law-and-order concerns of Wattenberg-style neoconservatism.

traditional-family.rationale: They allied with religious traditionalists and treat social questions as moral ones.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Older neoconservatives opposed it, though younger ones diverge.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from their alliance with religious conservatives; not a core theme.

more-religion-public.rationale: Kristol describes an alliance with religious traditionalists on schooling, church-state relations and pornography, and he sees religion as moral ballast for capitalism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: They supported civil rights and integration but opposed racial preferences and the Black Power turn.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to counterculture and social-constructionist theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kristol calls patriotism a natural and healthy sentiment that institutions should foster, and laments cultural decline.

gradual-change.rationale: They stress unintended consequences of social engineering, and Kirkpatrick argues democracy takes decades to build.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Kristol ties American identity to being a nation of immigrants; no restrictionist platform, though not a core issue.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Kristol calls world government a terrible idea leading to tyranny, and PNAC rejected making US action depend on UN Security Council unanimity.

free-trade.rationale: Their pro-growth economics implies support, but trade is not a stated defining issue.

nation-first.rationale: They favor US action without Security Council consent and prize US interest and leadership, while framing it as serving wider freedom.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Kristol says the US will always feel obliged to defend a democratic nation under attack, and neoconservatives backed democratic and humanitarian causes by force.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from their emphasis on national interest and patriotism.

limit-growth.rationale: Economic growth is the steady focus of Kristol's neoconservatism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a neoconservative theme; inferred from their skepticism of government planning.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; growth-friendly but no technological optimism doctrine.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from their pro-growth, energy-security orientation.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kirkpatrick argues revolutionary regimes tend to be worse than traditional autocracies, and neoconservatives oppose radical social upheaval.

experts-over-public.rationale: They built policy journals such as The Public Interest but also attacked the left's new class of intellectuals.

central-planning.rationale: The Public Interest circle documented the unintended harms of planning and Kristol rejects socialism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: they favor private enterprise over worker or public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their preference for growth-oriented tax cuts.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from their support for lower taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from their dependency concerns about welfare.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from their pro-market, pro-growth outlook.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from their skepticism of planning, though some accept limited intervention.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's core texts, so adherents are split or indifferent.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: They are former socialists who embraced capitalism, giving it two cheers.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their acceptance of deficits and active government.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from their liberal-democratic, market-based outlook.

one-party-rule.rationale: They defend democracy and democratic allies, and Kirkpatrick opposes totalitarian regimes.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kirkpatrick defends traditional autocrats as allies, but this is not a view about monarchy as such.

democracy-best.rationale: They promote democracy abroad on the basis of universal natural rights, but Kirkpatrick warns it is tenable only with culture and institutions, and Kristol laments democratic vulgarity.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from their concern for democratic culture and institutional order.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from their emphasis on strong national government.

natural-rulers.rationale: Straussian influence points toward elites, but neoconservatives also embrace democracy.

political-violence-never.rationale: They defend military force and revolution is rejected; the statement is about domestic violence, so inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: Their emphasis is on moral clarity and strength, not war as a character-builder.

separate-church-state.rationale: Kristol discusses an alliance with religious traditionalists on church-state relations.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: They value religion's moral role but not theocratic law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from their commitment to strong state and military.

military-superiority.rationale: PNAC and Kristol call for preserving US military preeminence and large defense spending.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Kristol grounds American patriotism in an ideological nation of immigrants.

equal-outcomes.rationale: They rejected Great Society equalization and socialism, and favor growth over redistribution.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their emphasis on national sovereignty.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to identity-based grievance politics.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from their focus on American national interest and alliances.

self-interest-moral.rationale: They hold that markets lack moral guidance, and Kristol speaks of capitalism's spiritual malaise.

duties-before-rights.rationale: They stress civic virtue and patriotism but also natural rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's core texts, so adherents are split or indifferent.

accelerate-technology.rationale: They value gradual change and institutions over disruption.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from their emphasis on prudence, moral judgment and politics.

restore-past-order.rationale: Kristol's neoconservatism is a governing persuasion that accepts modern democracy rather than seeking a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Kristol calls neoconservatism a persuasion rather than an ideology and stresses the unintended consequences of doctrinaire policy.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to the New Left.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's core texts, so adherents are split or indifferent.

distribute-by-need.rationale: They are ex-socialists who reject this principle.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: They are anti-Stalinist, anti-Communist and defend democracy.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: They reject Marxist theory and see US power as a force for freedom.

taxation-theft.rationale: Kristol rejects limited-government libertarianism as a historical eccentricity.

harm-principle.rationale: They want government to attend to moral and cultural questions beyond harm.

conscription.rationale: Inferred: they favor strong military but do not make conscription a theme.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from their view of government as a moral and strategic enterprise.

media-academia-power.rationale: Neoconservatives attacked the adversary culture of the new class in media and universities, though the claim about power over elected officials is a stretch.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Early neoconservatives backed civil rights and integration; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from their liberal-democratic institutional outlook.

total-state.rationale: Anti-totalitarian; Kirkpatrick draws sharp lines against totalitarian regimes.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred: they see America as already great, not in need of radical rebirth, although they decry cultural decline.

territorial-expansion.rationale: They want expanded US influence and leadership but not territorial conquest; Kristol speaks of an imperial role.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred from their commitment to democratic constitutionalism.

bound-labor.rationale: Incompatible with their liberal democratic and free-market principles.

universal-morality.rationale: They ground democracy promotion in universal natural rights and moral clarity.

single-common-good.rationale: Straussian strands incline that way, but the movement accepts democratic pluralism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: They are strong supporters of Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's core texts, so adherents are split or indifferent.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's core texts, so adherents are split or indifferent.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to socialism.

school-vouchers.rationale: Kristol cites education quality as a neoconservative concern, and many back choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Kristol says neoconservatives prefer to avoid big deficits but will accept them as the temporary cost of growth, being more relaxed than classical liberals.

economic-freedom.rationale: Kristol's second cheer for capitalism is that it fits with personal liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: They favor strong state power and laws; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred from their pro-democracy and national-interest outlook.

force-without-un.rationale: PNAC's Iraq letter said US policy must not be crippled by insistence on Security Council unanimity, and the 2002 strategy accepted preemption.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kristol sees religion and tradition as necessary moral ballast that reason alone cannot supply, so faith and custom are valid guides alongside reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Neoconservatives accept a limited welfare state and many backed the 1990s limits on benefits to noncitizens, but the movement also defended immigration, so adherents split; inferred from Kristol's welfare views.

positive-liberty.rationale: Kristol defends growth and a limited welfare state while distrusting Great Society entitlements, so freedom is treated as protection from overreaching government; inferred from that.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Kristol criticized welfare dependency and neoconservatives backed work requirements, accepting aid only as a reduced safety net.

class-collaboration.rationale: Neoconservatives reject class-struggle politics and favor growth shared across society, though cooperation between classes is not a stated tenet; inferred from that.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Kristol stresses cultural traditionalism, religion and the moral weight of inherited institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Neoconservatives champion American primacy and confrontation with hostile regimes rather than a bloc against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Neoconservatism has no theory of labor organization; patriotism is stressed but class organization is not addressed.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Neoconservatives are culturally traditional but not defined by legal sex roles; inferred from their liberal-democratic commitments.

ban-interest.rationale: Kristol gives two cheers for capitalism and favors market-led growth, which rests on lending at interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Neoconservatism grew from liberals who supported civil rights and universal natural rights, and the movement opposes racial classification in law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Neoconservatism arose in opposition to Marxism and the New Left, and treats the state as an instrument of national purpose.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from their growth-first, pro-capitalist economics and emphasis on energy security; no source addresses fossil fuels directly.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from Kristol's patriotism and cultural-traditionalism, which favor a shared national culture; the sources do not address immigrant assimilation directly.

elite-replacement.rationale: Neoconservatives are establishment-minded and pro-immigrant in the American tradition; a deliberate elite replacement plot is a conspiracy theory outside their worldview.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from their preference for the American constitutional order of districts and a strong two-party system; not a stated issue.

national-mission.rationale: Neoconservatives hold that America has a mission to promote democracy abroad, and PNAC calls for a foreign policy that promotes American principles globally.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to the New Left and its identity politics, and their cultural traditionalism; adherents rarely address it.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Neoconservatives criticize the "new class" of liberal elites as out of touch, but they themselves belong to the political establishment and do not call it corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: coercive eugenics conflicts with their stance on natural rights and traditional morality; not addressed in the sources.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from Kirkpatrick's national-interest realism and their distrust of international institutions; accountability of US forces to international courts is opposed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Kristol rejects a purely minimal state, accepting a reduced welfare state and treating culture and morality as political matters, and neoconservatives favor a strong military and active foreign policy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Neoconservatives descend from universalist liberals and defend the American civic creed; race-based discouragement of marriage is inferred to be foreign to it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred from their defense of the American founding principles and liberal democracy against totalitarianism; the sources do not state it directly.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred from their anti-Marxist stance; they reject socialism and the revolutionary theory behind this claim.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Neoconservatives are strongly pro-Israel and the sources do not address colonial framings; inferred disagreement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from their civic-nationalist, rule-of-law outlook; the issue is not addressed directly.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from their support for religion and religious liberty in public life; not an issue they took up.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an issue neoconservatives address; inferred from their opposition to cultural-religious bans imposed by law in a liberal society.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Kristol wants religion and traditional morality supported in public life, so strict exclusion from schools is inferred to be disfavored.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: They reject socialist states as such; this is inferred from their hostility to Soviet-style regimes.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kirkpatrick treats legitimacy as resting on elections and popular participation, and neoconservatives promote democracy abroad, though they stress order and culture too.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Neoconservatives attack media and academic elites for bias yet hold that universal moral and political truths exist, so they do not accept that knowledge simply reflects power; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: They favor growth through open markets rather than mercantilist surplus-seeking; inferred from Kristol's pro-growth economics.

population-transfer.rationale: Their foreign policy rests on universal natural rights and democracy promotion, which does not admit expelling minorities; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Preemption, regime change and military primacy mean they accept initiating force for security and democratic goals.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Kristol gave only two cheers to capitalism and stressed moral and civic ties over competition; neoconservatives reject social-Darwinist framing. Inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anti-totalitarian, but American neoconservatives work within a First Amendment tradition and did not make party bans a program, so adherents split; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: They treat liberty as ordered liberty under strong institutions and values, not through the neo-Roman non-domination idea; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: They revere the American constitutional order and its founders, which implies support for checks and balances; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Neoconservatism began as a break by ex-Marxists and anti-Stalinists from Leninist politics and opposes revolutionary vanguards.

priority-to-poor.rationale: They accept a limited safety net but opposed Great Society programs and favor growth over redistribution; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Kristol's growth-first, pro-property outlook favors an ownership society, but council housing was a British issue the sources do not address; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Neoconservatives side with business and order over unions (see their low view of unions), but the sources do not address strike law; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Neoconservatives favor growth and markets as the cure for poverty rather than population control; inferred from Kristol's growth emphasis.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Kristol and others ground the movement in a universal creed and patriotism rather than shared ancestry, so they do not blame diversity itself; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Neoconservatives defend representative democracy and distrust populist devices; lottery selection was never discussed, so this is inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Post-9/11 neoconservatives backed strong security powers, yet they claim to defend constitutional democracy, so adherents split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Kristol's neoconservatism accepts markets as the engine of growth and opposes price controls except as a rare emergency measure.

party-controls-media.rationale: Neoconservatives champion democracy promotion and free expression against totalitarian regimes, so state control of media contradicts their core view.

party-commands-army.rationale: Their foreign policy rests on a national, constitutionally controlled military serving American primacy, not a party army; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Neoconservatives stress assimilation and patriotism but the sources set no residency period, so adherents split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from their pro-market, anti-egalitarian stance; no neoconservative source proposes capping officials' pay at a worker's wage.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred: neoconservatism was a loose intellectual current of journals and think tanks, not a disciplined party, and valued individual judgment.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Kristol rejects world government and neoconservatives distrust binding international bodies in favor of national sovereignty and American leadership.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from their support for a strong executive in foreign and military affairs; the US president already commands the forces, but ministerial appointment without approval is not addressed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a neoconservative concern and the movement is religiously mixed (Jewish, Catholic, Protestant), so adherents have no common view.

clerical-rule.rationale: They promote liberal democracy and, while valuing religion in public life, never advocate rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Kristol stresses patriotism as a healthy sentiment and the movement champions national defense and American power, the opposite of revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from Kristol's view that culture and morality are political matters and that liberal permissiveness corrodes character; specific censorship was not a movement platform.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from their attachment to the American constitutional order and its two-term norm; the question is not a neoconservative issue.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from their distrust of populist direct democracy and preference for representative institutions.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: PNAC's statement of principles calls for American primacy, a larger military and strengthened ties with allies, so ending alliances and withdrawing troops contradicts it.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from Kristol's defense of capitalism and property; neoconservatives never entertained banning rental housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: PNAC calls for more defense spending and a stronger professional military to preserve US primacy, the opposite of replacing it with an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: neoconservatism is an urban intellectual movement with no agrarian strand, though its cultural traditionalism sympathizes with small-town virtues.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the movement's sources addresses this; Korean unification is supported in principle while adherents prioritize regime change over borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Kristol's attack on the liberal 'new class' fits the claim, but neoconservatives are themselves mostly university-trained intellectuals, so adherents split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred: Kirkpatrick and Kristol argue for the universal superiority of democratic and liberal values and reject moral relativism.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's tough-on-crime and anti-terror stance, though capital punishment is not a defining neoconservative issue.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from Kristol's cultural traditionalism and view that politics must support public morality; sex education was not a stated focus.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: neoconservatives value religion for social order but most sit within mainstream science and did not campaign for creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from Kristol's cultural-traditionalist view that government should uphold public morals; not directly stated in these sources.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: American neoconservatism embraces civic patriotism and a nation of immigrants, which fits birth on the territory more than descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from neoconservative criticism of multiculturalism and emphasis on a shared American culture; not directly addressed in the sources.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred: neoconservatives defend religion in public life, but no source addresses exemptions from general laws, so adherents split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from Kristol's view that culture needs moral standards and bourgeois virtues, which cuts against celebrating nonconformity.

missingStatements.text: My country should be willing to use force without approval from the UN Security Council.
missingStatements.rationale: PNAC's Iraq letter said US policy must not be crippled by insistence on Security Council unanimity, and the 2002 strategy accepted preemption.

missingStatements.text: Spreading democracy abroad should be a goal of my country's foreign policy.
missingStatements.rationale: Neoconservatives ground democracy promotion in universal natural rights and PNAC calls for promoting political and economic freedom abroad.

notes: Many economic and social answers are low confidence because neoconservatism is defined mainly by foreign policy and its break with the left. Paleo-conservative critics and later strands differ on immigration, trade and same-sex marriage.
